title: Clashes Erupt as Federal Forces Demolish Homes in Mogadishu's Tookiyo Neighbourhood Overnight; ~10 Hurt
detail: Federal security forces began demolishing homes in the Tookiyo area of Mogadishu's Yaqshiid district around midnight on Sunday, August 23, 2026, in an operation the government said was reclaiming state-owned land; the demolitions and ensuing confrontations with residents continued through the day. Security personnel and construction crews dismantled corrugated-iron roofing and structures as residents — who say they have lived in Tookiyo for decades — tried to block the operation, demanding clarity on its legal basis. Nearly ten people, including civilians, were injured in the clashes; unverified local reports indicated several young people were killed or wounded, but federal authorities had not released an official casualty toll as of August 24. Residents said government forces deployed DShK heavy machine guns during the confrontation, and Turkish Air Force F-16s — based at Aden Adde International Airport for the stated mission of supporting the fight against Al-Shabaab — flew low over Mogadishu, including over the affected area, during the operation; officials gave no explanation for the flights and there was no evidence the aircraft fired weapons or otherwise participated in the ground operation. It was the second time in 2026 Turkish F-16s were reported flying over the capital during a period of domestic unrest, after a similar flyover during opposition protests on May 10. Former presidents Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed 'Farmaajo' and Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed both publicly condemned the demolitions as forced displacement of families, elevating a local land dispute to national political significance and raising questions about whether Turkey's military footprint in Somalia risks becoming entangled in domestic political disputes. Hundreds of families face potential displacement, and residents voiced concern the operation could extend toward Suuq Bacaad, a major food market serving Mogadishu's northern districts.
